1.answer: A cluster commits a write when more than half of all its servers accept it.
1.quote: A cluster decides a change only when more than half of all its servers accept the change.

2.answer: Because with a smaller quorum, two groups in a network partition could both achieve quorum and decide different changes (split brain). A majority quorum ensures any two groups must overlap at some server.
2.quote: It happens because two groups of 2 among 4 servers need not share a server. So the quorum size must be more than half of n: then two groups cannot both decide.

4.answer: The group of 3 can still commit writes because 3 equals the majority requirement. The group of 2 cannot because 2 is less than the required 3.
4.quote: A, B, C have 3 accepts, and 3 ≥ 3, so they keep deciding. D and E have 2, and 2 < 3, so they stop.

stops: More than half of all n servers is the *majority size*: floor(n/2) + 1.
Two quorums each hold more than half of the servers, so together they list more than n servers. Some server must therefore be in both.
This depends on one assumption: a server remembers what it accepted, even after a restart.
Count more than half of *all* configured servers, failed or not.
This split of the network into groups that cannot reach each other is a *partition*.
For each position in that order, a server accepts only one change.
excess: Going from an even n to the next odd n keeps the majority size (4 → 5: both 3), so tolerance grows by 1.
That is why clusters usually have an odd number of servers.
Servers that lie need larger clusters.
A tolerance of 1 means a second failure stops the cluster.
A tolerance of 2 means one server can be off for an upgrade while another one fails.
The rest of this page explains why the rule must be "more than half".

The extra server only makes each change wait for one more accept.
